stages.label: Mataram at its height
stages.mapping_quality: approximate - draw as soft/hatched extent; regency borders did not exist and control was graded (core, tributary, contested)

polities.name: Mataram (directly held, incl. Madura from 1624, Surabaya from 1625)
polities.notes: Agung took Wirasaba 1615, Lasem 1616, Pasuruan 1617, Tuban 1619, Madura 1624, Surabaya 1625; Giri subdued c.1636. "Central and eastern Java plus Madura" is the standard summary. Malang/Lumajang/Probolinggo hinterland was thinly controlled. Mountainous south (Gunung Kidul, Pacitan) included by convention.
sources: M.C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c.1200 (4th ed., 2008), chs. 4-5, 8-11 (no URL; print)

polities.name: Blambangan (contested; campaigns 1635-39, submitted 1639, lost again 1659)
polities.notes: Conquered by Agung 1639-40 but never effectively held; Balinese (Gelgel) influence persisted; independent again by 1659.
sources: M.C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c.1200 (4th ed., 2008), chs. 4-5, 8-11 (no URL; print)

polities.name: Priangan (Sumedang, Ukur, Galuh, Sukapura) - Mataram vassal regencies
polities.notes: Sumedang submitted c.1620; Ukur/Sumedang revolts 1631-36 suppressed. Karawang was Mataram's forward base against Batavia (1630s). Cianjur/Subang/Purwakarta are approximations of a thinly populated frontier.
sources: M.C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c.1200 (4th ed., 2008), chs. 4-5, 8-11 (no URL; print)

polities.name: Cirebon (allied/vassal court)
polities.notes: Cirebon was subordinate to Mataram under Agung (marriage ties) but kept its own sultans. Majalengka/Indramayu boundary with Priangan is approximate.
sources: M.C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c.1200 (4th ed., 2008), chs. 4-5, 8-11 (no URL; print)

polities.name: Banten sultanate (west of the Cisadane)
polities.notes: Banten proper = Banten province; Bogor/Depok/Bekasi/Sukabumi were largely unpopulated hinterland in the 1630s (no clear owner).
sources: M.C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c.1200 (4th ed., 2008), chs. 4-5, 8-11 (no URL; print)

polities.name: VOC Batavia (founded 1619; besieged by Agung 1628-29)
polities.style: better drawn as a marker than an area: Batavia was a walled town plus a small ommelanden

polities.name: Unsettled borderland between Banten, Batavia and Mataram (Cisadane to Citarum)
polities.notes: Emptied by the wars of 1619-29; became Company land only by treaties with Mataram (1652) and Banten (1659, 1684). Mataram's de facto western edge was the Citarum (Karawang).

stages.label: The coast lost
stages.mapping_quality: medium - pasisir vs interior is defensible at regency scale; exact inland limit of VOC coastal districts is approximate

polities.name: Mataram (Kartasura, then Surakarta from 1745): Negaragung + Mancanagara
polities.notes: Negaragung = Mataram, Pajang, Sukowati, Kedu, Bagelen (DIY, Solo area, Magelang/Temanggung/Wonosobo, Purworejo/Kebumen). Mancanagara kulon = Banyumas area; Mancanagara wetan = Madiun, Kediri, Ponorogo, Pacitan, Jipang, Grobogan, Japan (Mojokerto), Wirasaba (Jombang) etc. NB: en.wikipedia (Mataram Sultanate) claims Mataram was reduced in 1743 to "areas around Surakarta, Yogyakarta, Kedu and Bagelen"; this contradicts the Giyanti lists (1755), which still divide the Mancanagara, so the Mancanagara are kept here. The interior was in civil war (Mangkubumi from 1746, Mas Said) - the court did not control all of it.
sources: M.C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c.1200 (4th ed., 2008), chs. 4-5, 8-11 (no URL; print)
M.C. Ricklefs, Jogjakarta under Sultan Mangkubumi 1749-1792 (1974), ch. on the Giyanti settlement and the 1774 boundary settlement (print)

polities.name: VOC (north coast/Pasisir ceded 1743, confirmed 1746; Madura after 1745-46)
polities.notes: Treaty of (Nov.) 1743 after the Chinese War: VOC sovereignty over the north coast, Madura and the east (Oosthoek). Wikipedia (Java War 1741-43) gives "northern coast of Java, Madura and eastern Java". The contract of 18 May 1746 is cited in the Giyanti text as the cession instrument. West Java/Priangan and Cirebon were already VOC (1677-1705). Blambangan (east tip) was only actually conquered 1767-72: hatch it. Madura: eastern Madura (Sumenep, Pamekasan) ceded 1705; western Madura (Cakraningrat IV) taken 1745-46. 11 Nov 1743 cession (Surabaya, Rembang, Jepara, West Madura, the pasisir) and 18 May 1746 lease of the remaining coast; the 11 Dec 1749 cession of the whole realm was on paper while the interior was in revolt.
sources: M.C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c.1200 (4th ed., 2008), chs. 4-5, 8-11 (no URL; print)

polities.name: Semarang hinterland (VOC or Mataram - uncertain)
polities.notes: VOC fort at Salatiga (De Hersteller, 1746) and Ungaran; the 1757 treaty was signed in Salatiga. Draw neutral or with VOC hatch.
sources: M.C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c.1200 (4th ed., 2008), chs. 4-5, 8-11 (no URL; print)

polities.name: Surapati's descendants (Malang and Lumajang) until the VOC campaigns of 1767-71
sources: M.C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c.1200 (4th ed., 2008), chs. 4-5, 8-11 (no URL; print)

polities.name: Banten (VOC vassal)
sources: M.C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c.1200 (4th ed., 2008), chs. 4-5, 8-11 (no URL; print)

polities.name: Blambangan under Balinese (Mengwi) overlordship; VOC claim from 1743 on paper only
polities.notes: VOC conquest only 1767-68, pacified 1771-72.

stages.label: Giyanti and Salatiga
stages.mapping_quality: NOT faithfully mappable at regency level. Recommended: draw the whole S2 Mataram area as one "Vorstenlanden" block hatched in both court colours ("divided, interlocking"), optionally tinting only the Mancanagara blocks below by dominant court. Mangkunegaran as a hatched overlay on Karanganyar/Wonogiri.

polities.name: Negaragung - split field by field between Surakarta and Yogyakarta (intermixed)
polities.confidence: high (that it is intermixed) / n.a. (for any line)
polities.style: cross-hatch both court colours; optionally darken Yogyakarta colour toward DIY and Surakarta colour toward Kota Surakarta/Sukoharjo/Boyolali
polities.notes: Yogyakarta's Negaragung: Siti Gadhing Mataram (between Merapi and the sea), Siti Bumija (Kedu, Progo to Merbabu), Siti Numbakanyar (Bagelen, between Bagawanta and Progo), Siti Panekar (east Pajang down to Gunungkidul), Siti Ageng Mlayakusuma (east Pajang). Surakarta held the corresponding shares in Pajang, Sukowati, Kedu and Bagelen. Lands "saling tercampur aduk dan berdempetan" (Hakim 2019, citing Purwadi & Waryanti 2015) - only the 1830 Klaten agreement drew a line (Opak river / Prambanan road).
sources: A.L. Hakim, "Penyatuan wilayah enclave (Imogiri, Kotagede, dan Ngawen) ke dalam DIY 1948-1960", Jurnal Prodi Ilmu Sejarah UNY 4(1), 2019, pp. 90-97: https://journal.student.uny.ac.id/ilmu-sejarah/article/download/14710/14273
M.C. Ricklefs, Jogjakarta under Sultan Mangkubumi 1749-1792 (1974), ch. on the Giyanti settlement and the 1774 boundary settlement (print)

polities.name: Yogyakarta - Mancanagara (dominant)
polities.notes: Lists (id.wikipedia Kesultanan Yogyakarta; Hakim 2019): Madiun, Magetan, Caruban (Madiun regency), half of Pacitan, Kertosono, Berbek, Kalangbret, Ngrowo (Tulungagung), Japan (Mojokerto), Jipang (Bojonegoro), Teras Karas (Ngawen, Blora), Sela, Warung (Kuwu-Wirosari) and part of Grobogan, plus ~1,600 karya in Banyumas (Danureja I). Total 33,950 cacah.
sources: A.L. Hakim, "Penyatuan wilayah enclave (Imogiri, Kotagede, dan Ngawen) ke dalam DIY 1948-1960", Jurnal Prodi Ilmu Sejarah UNY 4(1), 2019, pp. 90-97: https://journal.student.uny.ac.id/ilmu-sejarah/article/download/14710/14273
M.C. Ricklefs, Jogjakarta under Sultan Mangkubumi 1749-1792 (1974), ch. on the Giyanti settlement and the 1774 boundary settlement (print)

polities.name: Surakarta - Mancanagara (dominant)
polities.notes: id.wikipedia Kasunanan Surakarta lists Mancanagara kulon: Banyumas, Bantar (Brebes), Lebaksiu/Balapulang (Tegal), Jabarangkah (Batang), Kalibeber (Wonosobo), Karanganyar/Karangbolong (Kebumen), Merden/Karangkobar (Banjarnegara), Bobotsari/Kertanegara (Purbalingga); Mancanagara wetan: Jogorogo (Ngawi), Ponorogo, Kaduwang (Wonogiri), Pacitan, Tulungagung, Kediri, Pace and Berbek (Nganjuk), Wirasaba (Jombang), Japan, Madiun, Magetan, Caruban. That wetan list overlaps the Yogyakarta list (Madiun, Magetan, Caruban, Japan, Tulungagung) - either it describes pre-1755 Kasunanan or shared districts; treat overlaps as Yogyakarta-dominant with Surakarta enclaves. 32,350 cacah.
sources: A.L. Hakim, "Penyatuan wilayah enclave (Imogiri, Kotagede, dan Ngawen) ke dalam DIY 1948-1960", Jurnal Prodi Ilmu Sejarah UNY 4(1), 2019, pp. 90-97: https://journal.student.uny.ac.id/ilmu-sejarah/article/download/14710/14273
M.C. Ricklefs, Jogjakarta under Sultan Mangkubumi 1749-1792 (1974), ch. on the Giyanti settlement and the 1774 boundary settlement (print)

polities.name: Mancanagara districts split between both courts
polities.notes: Pacitan explicitly halved; Nganjuk: Kertosono/Berbek to Yogyakarta, Pace to Surakarta; Trenggalek not named in any list consulted (likely split between Ponorogo and Ngrowo appanages) - draw hatched. Ngawi: Jogorogo (south) to Surakarta, Ngawi proper to Yogyakarta.

polities.name: Mangkunegaran (1757, 4,000 karya/cacah, carved from Surakarta)
polities.notes: Salatiga treaty art. 7: 4,000 karya in Kaduwang, Nglaroh, Matesih, Wiroko, Haribaya, Honggobayan, Sembuyan, Gunung Kidul, Kedu and Pajang (north and south). Kaduwang/Nglaroh/Wiroko/Sembuyan lie in Wonogiri, Matesih/Haribaya/Honggobayan in Karanganyar; the Gunung Kidul, Kedu and Pajang parcels were scattered. In 1757 it did not yet cover the full modern regencies. Also small parcels in Gunungkidul (Ngawen), Pajang and Kedu (not drawn).

polities.name: VOC
polities.notes: Giyanti art. 6: Sultan renounces Madura and the coast ceded in 1746 (receives 10,000 real/yr). Blambangan still contested (Bali) until 1767-72; Malang until 1767-71.

polities.name: Outside VOC/court control (Blambangan, Malang)
sources: M.C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c.1200 (4th ed., 2008), chs. 4-5, 8-11 (no URL; print)

polities.style: small hatched patch / marker - NOT the whole of Kulon Progo
polities.notes: 4,000 cacah, initially scattered, consolidated as Karang Kemuning (Adikarto from 1877) = modern kapanewon Temon, Wates, Panjatan, Galur (Avatara 2019); drawn in its consolidated form.

polities.name: Annexed by the British/Dutch government 1811-12 (Kedu; Japan, Jipang, Grobogan, half Pacitan from Yogyakarta; Surakarta's shares likewise)
polities.notes: id.wikipedia Kesultanan Yogyakarta: British took Kedu, half Pacitan, Japan, Jipang and Grobogan after the Geger Sepehi (June 1812). Blora and Jombang (Wirasaba) for Surakarta are inferred (low). Wonosobo (Ledok) was annexed only in 1830 and joined Kedu in 1901 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kedu_Residency).

polities.name: Pacitan: Yogyakarta's half ceded to the British 1812, Surakarta's half kept (its status uncertain)

adm2_part.Kota Surakarta: southern part (Pasar Kliwon, Serengan, Laweyan, most of Jebres) - north (Banjarsari) was Mangkunegaran
adm2_part.Bantul: enclaves Kotagede SK (Jagalan, Singosaren, Segoroyoso, Bawuran, Wonolelo, Terong, Jatimulyo) and Imogiri SK (Imogiri, Girirejo, Karangtalun, Karangtengah, Kebonagung, Dlingo, Mangunan, Muntuk, Temuwuh)

polities.notes: Klaten agreement: Pajang and Sukowati to the Sunan, Mataram and Gunungkidul to the Sultan; line along the Opak river, later the road from Prambanan north to Merapi and south to the Gunungkidul foothills. Sunan kept 500 cacah around the Kotagede/Imogiri graves; Sultan kept 12 jung at the Selo graves (Grobogan, government land).
